text:
Dear Dr. Morrison,

Thank you for evaluating Ms. Elena Vance, a 42-year-old administrative assistant referred for further ophthalmic assessment. Her visual concerns date back to early childhood, when she initially developed notable trouble navigating in dim lighting and dark environments. Over the intervening years, she has experienced progressive decline in central clarity, with current corrected acuity measuring 20/80 in the right eye and 20/70 in the left. 

On anterior segment examination, she demonstrates bilateral posterior subcapsular lens opacities, though her corneas and anterior chambers are clear, and intraocular pressures are normal at 15 mmHg bilaterally. She is on no regular prescription medications and her general medical history is unremarkable.

Dilated funduscopy reveals pronounced waxy pallor of both optic nerve heads along with severe narrowing and thinning of the retinal vascular tree. In the mid-periphery, there are extensive bone-corpuscle pigment clumps distributed circumferentially. Prior electrophysiological testing corroborates an advanced process with marked combined loss of both rod and cone photoreceptor responses. Of note, peripheral inspection confirmed no scalloped patches of chorioretinal thinning, and there are no signs of intraocular inflammation.

I would be very grateful for your subspecialist opinion regarding her visual prognosis and any supportive management strategies you might recommend.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Sterling
